claims.text: The FDA label says alcoholic beverages with tinidazole may cause abdominal cramps, nausea, vomiting, headaches, and flushing.
claims.quote: Alcohols, Disulfiram: Alcoholic beverages and preparations containing ethanol or propylene glycol should be avoided during tinidazole therapy and for 3 days afterward because abdominal cramps, nausea, vomiting, headaches, and flushing may occur.

claims.text: A systematic review describes available data as supporting concomitant tinidazole and alcohol use.
claims.quote: tinidazole, and fluconazole can be safely used with concomitant alcohol consumption.

headline.text: The FDA tinidazole label warns of cramps, nausea, vomiting, headaches, and flushing with alcohol.

reported.text: The FDA label describes adverse reactions with alcohol, while a systematic review describes available data as supporting concomitant use.
